summary: Order placement failures are most likely caused by the external broker API rate-limiting broker-gateway with HTTP 429. broker-gateway then returns 503 to order-router and orchestrator, and order-router returns 503 to web-app. broker-gateway's rate_limit_remaining reached 0.0 and its err_rate peaked at 0.407, while its rps stayed flat at 37.56-42.686, so the quota was exhausted without a traffic spike on our side. Orchestrator 503s start at 11:55:51, about 4.5 minutes before the first logged 429 at 12:00:20, so the logs do not show exactly how it began; the error log was truncated at 50 of 309 entries. Postgres and rabbitmq are healthy, and the only changes in the window were minor deploys (wa-webhook, web-app) that don't match the failures. Portfolio sync and the slow assistant are not explained yet: I didn't check llm-gateway, portfolio-svc or aa-sync directly.

hypotheses.statement: The external broker API rate-limits broker-gateway (429), which exhausts rate_limit_remaining. broker-gateway then returns 503 to order-router and orchestrator, and order-router returns 503 to web-app, causing the order placement failures.
hypotheses.label: medium

supporting.text: broker-gateway is receiving 429 rate-limit responses from the broker API
web-app sees order-router 503s, so the failure propagates upstream
broker-gateway rate_limit_remaining hit 0 and err_rate rose to 0.407
broker-gateway request rate is flat, so there was no traffic spike on our side
broker-gateway is called by order-router (weight 0.8) and orchestrator (weight 0.3)

contradicting.text: Orchestrator was already seeing broker-gateway 503s before the first logged 429

hypotheses.statement: The slow assistant and portfolio sync failures come from a separate problem, or from retry and latency effects of the broker failures. The evidence cannot separate these.
hypotheses.label: low

actions.text: Check the broker API quota and plan limits and contact the broker about the 429s. Reduce or queue order calls to broker-gateway and honour retry-after 30s with backoff and jitter.
actions.rationale: rate_limit_remaining is 0 and the broker is returning 429s with retry-after 30s, which drives the 503s to order-router and orchestrator.

actions.text: Identify who else consumes the broker API quota (other keys, batch jobs, retry storms) and check whether the broker changed its limits around 11:55-12:00.
actions.rationale: Our rps is flat, so the exhaustion is not explained by our traffic. Orchestrator 503s also start before the first logged 429.

actions.text: Investigate the portfolio sync failures (aa-sync, portfolio-svc) and the assistant latency (llm-gateway, orchestrator) with targeted logs and metrics.
actions.rationale: These symptoms are not explained by the broker rate limit evidence, and postgres and portfolio-consumer look healthy.

actions.text: Add alerting on broker-gateway rate_limit_remaining and a circuit breaker or graceful degradation message for order placement.
actions.rationale: Quota exhaustion was only visible through downstream 503s.
